name: Modern SEO M1 L4: How We Do Local SEO
body:
> Module 1, 3:43. Source: Lesson 4 How We Do Local SEO.mp4

## In short
- Measurement comes first: before touching a client's website or GBP, set up a rank map that runs every other week for "primary category + city name," at minimum. It is the "North Star."
- Every new client starts with the 3-step system: GBP audit and fix, GBP landing page audit and fix, source quality citations. Then join the Chamber of Commerce.
- If the rank map is below the green target (20 to 40% in audio, 30 to 40% on the slides), add 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month. If that is still not enough, start the Core 30 process.
- Core 30 builds topical relevance (a page for every GBP category and service, linked to match the GBP). After that, shift to geographic relevance (service area content).
- Each phase builds on the last: fundamentals before advanced content, topical relevance before geographic expansion.

## Key ideas
- **Measurement is the foundation.** The rank map shows where the client ranks and how far from the address they reach the top 3. It tells you whether the work is working and when to move to the next phase. (0:18 to 0:43, slide at 0:25)
- **The 3-step system for all new clients** (slide at 1:05): GBP audit and fix, GBP landing page audit and fix, source quality citations. "This handles the basics that most businesses get wrong." (0:49)
- **Chamber of Commerce as a trust link.** Joining gives "a high-quality local authority link that Google recognizes as a trust signal." (1:06)
- **Green threshold decides the next step.** Check the rank map for top 3 areas. The audio says less than "20, 30, 40% green areas, depending on the size of the city." The slides say 30 to 40%. Below that, start sourcing 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month. (1:13, slide at 1:25)
- **Core 30 if links are not enough.** If the 3 steps plus local links do not reach the green target, start Core 30 (covered in Module 3). In short: build a page for every GBP category and service, and link them the same way they are structured on the GBP, so the website and GBP match. This builds "a massive amount of topical relevance." (1:38 to 2:08, slides at 1:45 and 2:05)
- **Then geographic relevance.** Once the map reaches the green target, Google knows what you provide and trusts you, so switch to teaching Google about all your service areas. (2:13 to 2:26)
- **Link every new page.** For every new content page, source "a decent link" to help get it indexed faster. Google needs to see the content is worth crawling and indexing. (2:31, slide at 2:45)
- **Ongoing trust.** Throughout the whole process, keep sourcing 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month so the GBP ranks farther from the address. (2:40)
- **Repeat until green.** Keep going until the rank map shows green coverage across the target area and the client ranks top 3 for the primary keyword across a wide radius. (2:53, slide at 3:05)
- **Order matters.** No advanced content until fundamentals are handled. No geographic expansion until strong topical relevance is in place. (3:05, slide at 3:25)

## Step-by-step process
The agency roadmap, in the instructor's order:
1. Set up a local rank map that runs every other week for the primary category + city name keyword (at minimum), before changing anything. (0:21)
2. Step 1 of the 3-step system: GBP audit and fix. (0:54)
3. Step 2: GBP landing page audit and fix. (0:56)
4. Step 3: source quality citations. (0:59)
5. Join the local Chamber of Commerce for a local authority link. (1:06)
6. Check the rank map. Are there top 3 areas? (1:13)
7. If green is below the target (20 to 40% by city size in audio, 30 to 40% on slide), source 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month. Use the course's Prompt Library prompt to find opportunities in any city. (1:19 to 1:32)
8. If the 3 steps plus local links still do not reach the target, start Core 30: a page for every GBP category and service, linked to mirror the GBP structure. (1:38 to 2:02)
9. Once the map reaches the target, shift to geographic relevance: content about all the service areas. (2:13 to 2:26)
10. For every new content page, source a decent link to speed up indexing. (2:31)
11. Keep sourcing 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month throughout. (2:40)
12. Repeat until the rank map shows green coverage across the target area. (2:53)

## Checklist
- Rank map set up before any changes.
- Rank map runs every other week.
- Rank map keyword includes at least primary category + city name.
- GBP audited and fixed.
- GBP landing page audited and fixed.
- Quality citations sourced.
- Chamber of Commerce membership and link in place.
- Rank map green percentage checked against the target for the city size.
- 1 to 2 high-trust local links sourced each month (if below target, and ongoing throughout).
- Core 30 started only if the 3 steps plus links are not enough.
- Every GBP category and service has its own page, linked the way the GBP is structured.
- Geographic (service area) content started only after the topical target is reached.
- Every new content page gets a decent link to help indexing.

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| Local rank map | North Star metric, run every other week | 0:25 |
| 3-step system | Foundation for all new clients (detailed in Lesson 5) | 0:49 |
| Chamber of Commerce | High-quality local authority (trust) link | 1:06 |
| Prompt Library (course resource) | A prompt to find high-trust local link opportunities in any city | 1:32 |
| Core 30 process | Topical relevance build, covered in Module 3 | 1:46 |

## Numbers and benchmarks
These are the instructor's claims, not verified facts.
- Rank map frequency: every other week. (0:25)
- Green target before adding links: "20, 30, 40%, depending on the size of the city" in audio. The slides at 1:25 and 1:45 say "30-40%." (1:19, 1:38, 2:13)
- High-trust local links: 1 to 2 per month, both when below target and ongoing. (1:27, 2:40)
- One "decent link" per new content page. (2:31)

## Terms
**Rank map (North Star):** A recurring grid rank check for primary category + city that guides every decision.
**Green areas:** Rank map points where the client is in the top 3.
**3-step system:** GBP audit and fix, GBP landing page audit and fix, source quality citations.
**High-trust local link:** A link from a trusted local source (for example the Chamber of Commerce).
**Core 30 process:** Building a page for every GBP category and service and linking them the same way they are structured on the GBP, so the site and GBP match.
**Topical relevance:** Google understanding what services the business provides and in what detail.
**Geographical relevance:** Google understanding all the service areas where the business provides those services.

## Worth quoting
- "The foundation of everything we do is measurement." (0:18)
- "This rank map becomes our North Star." (0:40)
- "We don't focus on geographical expansion until we've established a strong topical relevance." (3:12)

## How to use this at TAG
- **Rank map first.** For Pipeliners, Alphalete, and Summit AZ, confirm there is a rank map running every other week on primary category + city before planning new work. If TAG does not have a grid rank tool, flag it to Kim rather than signing up for one (memory file `feedback_no_paid_services.md`).
- **Place each client on the roadmap.** For each client, mark which phase they are in (3 steps, local links, Core 30, geographic) based on their rank map green percentage. That tells Kim what the next task is.
- **Compare TAG's link plan to the lesson.** TAG's standing decisions include 2 press releases per month and $50 per month per client in backlinks through Search Atlas (memory file `project_tag_meeting_decisions.md`). The lesson calls specifically for 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month, such as the Chamber of Commerce. Kim may want to check whether current links are local and high-trust.
- **Chamber of Commerce.** Recommend that Kim check whether each client is a member of its local chamber and has a listing that links to the site.
- **Links for indexing.** The lesson says each new page needs a decent link to get indexed. Alphalete has had trouble getting its many city pages indexed (memory file `project_alphalete_gsc_indexing.md`). This lesson supports linking to new pages (internal and external) as part of the fix.
- **Order of work.** Hold off on service area expansion pages for a client until its service and category pages (topical relevance) are in place and the map is near the green target.
- The green-coverage example slide at 3:05 shows a Phoenix metro map (Phoenix, Scottsdale, and Mesa labels visible). It is a useful picture of the end goal for Summit AZ's market, though it is not identified as any particular client.

## Open questions
- **Green target conflict.** The audio says 20, 30, or 40% depending on city size. The slides say 30 to 40%. No rule was given for which city size maps to which number.
- **Lesson order.** Lesson 1 previewed this content as "Lesson 3." It is Lesson 4 in the files.
- **Prompt Library prompt** is mentioned but not shown. Kim would need to find it in the course resources.
- **"Decent link"** for new pages is not defined (quality level or source).
- The 3-step system wording here ("GBP landing page audit and fix," "source quality citations") differs slightly from Lesson 5 ("GBP landing page audit," "super citations"). They appear to be the same steps.
- No low-confidence transcript lines.

## Timestamps
- 0:03 A systematic, methodical process for every client
- 0:18 Measurement first: rank map every other week
- 0:40 Rank map as the North Star
- 0:49 The 3-step system for all new clients
- 1:06 Join the Chamber of Commerce
- 1:13 Check the rank map; green threshold; 1 to 2 local links per month
- 1:32 Prompt Library prompt for local link opportunities
- 1:38 Core 30 process (Module 3)
- 2:13 Shift to geographical relevance
- 2:31 A decent link for every new content page
- 2:40 Ongoing 1 to 2 high-trust local links per month
- 2:53 Repeat until green coverage across the target area
- 3:05 Each phase builds on the previous one
- 3:27 Next lesson: the 3-step method
